Subject: Clarify: overage / buffer band language for multi-year prepay

Hi Vanessa —

Thanks again for the term sheet this morning. Two quick clarifying questions from procurement before we share with legal:  

1) The "buffer band" in Section 4.2 — is that applied per-year or measured across the entire multi-year commitment? Our budget team wants to understand whether the 10% band is per contract year (so they can use it against annual budgets) or if it aggregates over the 3-year commitment.

2) If we go above prepaid units in a year but stay within the buffer band, do those excess tokens roll forward to the next year or are they considered consumed? Also: what rate applies to overage above the buffer band — the base per-token rate, or a higher overage rate?

We'd like a short written confirmation we can attach to the purchase order.

Anna —

Thanks for the clear questions. Short answers up front, then some context below so legal/procurement have a single place to reference.

1) Buffer band is applied per contract year by default. For a 3-year prepay we treat each 12-month period independently for the band calculation. If you prefer an aggregate (annualized across the whole term) we can discuss but it changes the math for discounts.

2) Excess usage within the buffer band is counted as consumed against that year's prepay (it does not roll forward). Overage above the buffer band triggers the overage rate in the pricing table; we propose a stepped overage: standard overage = 1.2x base per-token rate for the first 20% above the band, then 1.1x beyond that (volume break). This is intended to be predictable and still encourage accurate forecasting.

I'm cc'ing Rishi (deal lead), Laura (legal), and Ben (finance) to weigh in. I'll attach an updated term sheet and a small usage workbook so you can see example scenarios.

Next steps: if procurement is OK with the per-year band and non-rollforward policy we'll add the clarifying sentence to Section 4.2 and include example calculations in the P.O. addendum.

Team —

Quick internal run-through after Vanessa's reply and a quick look at the workbook she shared. High level comments:

- Agree per-year buffer band keeps finance modeling simple for Clarity; they'll reconcile annually with their P&L.
- Recommend we offer an optional "aggregate true-down" for Year 3 only (customer can elect at signing). This would allow underutilization in Years 1–2 to offset Year 3 overages at a blended rate — useful for customers with front-loaded onboarding. If we offer this, discount tiers for the entire term should be adjusted slightly (we can keep headline discount but with a +1% margin).
- Overage cadence: propose annual true-down (30 days after year-end) with a carry-forward explicitly disallowed unless opt-in. Carry-forward creates revenue recognition complexity.

Pricing proposal for inclusion in the term sheet (sample):
- Buffer band: 10% of annual prepaid units (per year)
- Within-band: considered consumed (no rebate / no carry-forward)
- Overage 0–20% above band: 1.20x base per-token
- Overage >20%: 1.10x base per-token (volume break applies to the >20% portion)

If LAURA can draft the exact clause language I can sign off and Vanessa can circulate to Clarity. Ben — any objections from a recognition/cash perspective?

Anna / team —

I've drafted language below that captures the intent discussed by Sales/Finance. Please review and let me know if you'd like any edits; this is intentionally prescriptive so procurement doesn't need to chase interpretations. We can insert this as a new paragraph in Section 4.2 (True-up; Overage).

"Buffer band and true-up. For each Contract Year, Customer shall be entitled to usage up to the Annual Prepaid Units plus a Buffer Band equal to ten percent (10%) of such Annual Prepaid Units. Usage within the Buffer Band shall be deemed consumed and shall not be eligible for credit or carry-forward to subsequent Contract Years. Within thirty (30) days following the end of each Contract Year, the parties shall perform an annual true-up. Any Usage in excess of the Annual Prepaid Units plus the Buffer Band shall be invoiced as Overage. Overage shall be charged at the applicable Overage Rate as set forth in the Pricing Table. The parties may elect, at the time of execution, an Aggregate True-Down option that applies only in the final Contract Year and permits underutilization in prior years to offset overages in the final year at a blended rate determined by Redwood. Carry-forward of excess prepaid units is not permitted except where specifically agreed in writing in an Addendum signed by both parties."

A couple of practical notes:
- The "aggregate true-down" clause is a customer-friendly optional add-on; if Clarity chooses it we should adjust the discount margin (Rishi's +1% is reasonable).
- We should explicitly call out how invoices will show the overage calculation (line items: prepaid, buffer, overage bands) to reduce PO/AR back-and-forth.

If acceptable, Vanessa can send this back to procurement and I'll prepare the short redline to the PDF.

Thanks,

Anna —

Thanks for the patience. Per our internal review we've agreed to the following (summary for procurement/legal):

1) Buffer band: 10% per contract year (applies each 12-month period independently).
2) Within-band usage: counted as consumed, not eligible for carry-forward or credit.
3) Overage calculation: annual true-up within 30 days after each Contract Year. Overage invoiced per the Pricing Table with stepped bands: 1.20x base rate for the first 0–20% above the band; 1.10x base rate for amounts greater than 20% above the band (applied to the excess portion).
4) Aggregate True-Down (optional): customer may elect an Aggregate True-Down that applies only to the final contract year; electing this option will result in a small adjustment to the effective discount (we propose adding 1% to the term margin).
5) Carry-forward: not allowed unless explicitly agreed in a signed addendum.

I've attached the updated term sheet (v4) with the redline to Section 4.2 and the usage workbook with three scenarios (flat usage, ramped onboarding, and front-loaded spike) so you can see how invoices would compute. If procurement is comfortable with the per-year band and non-rollforward posture, please confirm and we will include the final clause in the P.O. addendum and proceed to signature.

If you'd like a quick call to walk through the workbook, Rishi and I are available tomorrow afternoon.
